content:
maria (support): Heads up — customer reported streaming tool-call args getting chopped in the middle of JSON, which causes our schema validator to blow up and the tool never runs. They see a 400 from our tool-proxy with 'invalid_json' and a later 'tool_call_failed'\.

eli (eng): ugh, can you paste the raw streaming output they captured? is this coming from function-calling or a custom tool framing? :eyes:

maria (support): Here's the customer's snippet (we redacted identifiers). They set `stream: true` and are using the model function-calling flow. The model starts a tool call but the streamed payload ends mid-object:

```
<<stream-chunk-1>>: {"name":"lookup_account","arguments":"{"account_id":"acct_42","filters":["active","legacy"],"include":{"billing":true,"contacts":["primary","
<<stream-chunk-2>>: secondary"]},"meta":{"request_id":"rq_abc123"} }"}
# note: last chunk seems to have been cut at 'secondary' and the JSON never closed
```

maria (support): They tried `stream:false` and it works (complete JSON, tool runs). Any idea why streaming would cut mid-JSON?

ben (runtime): Thanks for the repro. Two things to check: 1) whether the streaming connection is being terminated by some intermediate proxy due to buffer/idle/timeouts, 2) whether our stream-assembler is applying an early parse when it sees what looks like JSON but hasn't reached the end-of-object.

eli (eng): Ben — on the runtime we have a piece that attempts to parse function args as they arrive so we can start the tool early for lower latency. If that parser gets a partial top-level token that looks valid but isn't closed, it should wait, but there was an old change that treated `]}` as end-of-args heuristics when chunks contain nested arrays/objects. Could be a bug when a quoted string contains `]` or `}` inside content that gets split.

maria (support): Customer supplied request details:
- request_id: rq_abc123 (in the payload)
- external request token: tok_xxx (we redacted)
- model: gpt-x-large (via Redwood catalog)
- timestamp: 2025-09-18T14:05:12Z
- stream: true

maria (support): They said it happens ~10% of their streams. Usually long argument payloads (nested contact lists, long notes).

eli (eng): Repro steps I want to run locally:
1) Use model + function spec matching `lookup_account`
2) Call with `stream: true` and a generated arg blob containing nested arrays + quoted strings that include `]` and `}` and long text to try to force chunk boundaries inside strings
3) Capture server-side stream assembly logs for request id and look for `assemble-chunk` and `parse-attempt` events

ben (runtime): I'll add a debug flag to the stream assembler to log chunk boundaries and the partial buffer before any parse attempt. For now workarounds for customers:
- set `stream: false` if immediate fix required
- or change tool args to base64-encode large free-text fields (less ergonomic)
- or add an explicit final sentinel token that the model emits as the last token before closing the JSON, e.g., "__END_JSON__", then we wait for sentinel before parsing.

maria (support): Customer prefers not to decode base64. They want a platform fix. Asking if we can roll a hotfix.

eli (eng): I think a small runtime change should help: never attempt to parse arguments until we detect a closing brace at top-level AND the buffer is not ending in an open-quote. Safer approach: always attempt parse only when we see a non-escaped `}` that balances braces to zero. I can prototype a patch that defers parse until brace depth returns to zero or a sentinel observed.

ben (runtime): Agreed. Also will check for premature stream termination — our ingress NGINX has a default 30s idle timeout; if some clients have slow token production that could close the connection and truncate the last chunk. I'll verify idle timeouts in front of the assembler and increase or apply keepalive.

deploy-bot: Scheduled new canary: runtime/stream-assembler v2025.10.2-canary -> infra-canary-1 at 2025-09-18T15:30:00Z :rocket:

eli (eng): For triage, can support attach the full request/response logs (redacted) and the customer's sample payload? I need the raw chunk boundaries captured on the customer side — they included a `chunks.log` earlier in the ticket but it's partial. Also include HTTP request id from Redwood (x-rw-request-id header) so we can correlate.

maria (support): Yep, I've asked the customer for their `chunks.log` and the full x-rw-request-id. I've also offered `stream:false` as a temporary workaround and scheduled them for a follow-up after the canary deploy.

eli (eng): Plan: 1) add guard in stream-assembler to only attempt JSON parse when top-level brace depth is zero and not inside an open string; 2) add debug dump for chunk boundaries; 3) increase idle keepalive between NGINX and assembler; 4) deploy canary and validate with customer sample. If canary looks good we'll promote.

ben (runtime): I'll own the canary and rollback playbook if we see regressions. maria, please ping me when you have the x-rw-request-id.

maria (support): Will do. Thanks team — I'll update the customer and post their logs once they arrive. :thumbsup:

eli (eng): One more note for support replies: mention that this is a streaming assembly bug (not model hallucination) and that non-streaming is a reliable workaround. Also include our timeline — canary within a few hours, rollback plan, and contact for urgent escalation.

maria (support): Got it, sending update now.
